blindSummary: This unit was covered by the dedicated country-level dossier, which found no region-specific change to the national position that merits a separate assessment; the local picture follows the national framework described above.
blindSourceSummaries: News feature (Jan 2018) on transgender women in prison: transgender women incarcerated on the basis of their legal gender fall into a legal grey area and are punished for far more than their alleged crimes - first-person accounts of placement in an all-male facility (a three-day stay in a men's prison in 2014, with detainee and staff hostility; a foreign trans woman's story of incarceration); a criminal procedure provision assigns detainees by the sex on their ID; the national prison inspectorate says transgender detainees are the group that 'suffers the most' in prison; also covers a well-publicised case of a trans woman detained in poor conditions after a 2016 protest.

Official opinion of 25 May 2021 of the national prison inspectorate on the treatment of transgender persons in all places of deprivation of liberty: built on about forty referrals received since 2010, interviews with trans associations and external experts, and five on-site inspections (men's and women's prisons, a remand facility and a central police station across the country - eight trans women and one trans man interviewed); finds persistent serious violations of fundamental rights of trans detainees, isolation and overcrowding risks; recommends that the 2016 depathologising law (no more surgery requirement for civil-status change) be translated into prison regulations; explicitly extends to intersex and non-binary people.

Anti-torture organisation news blog (interview extract with the national preventive mechanism on its 25 May 2021 opinion): trans persons deprived of liberty face the constant risk of violence, discrimination and abuse; the 2010 Opinion was insufficient given no improvement in places of detention; the new Opinion followed five dedicated inspection visits across regions and institution types; findings include no public data on trans detainees, no staff training, few national guidelines, and the 2016 depathologisation law not applied to places of detention.
blindLocalsOnly: The placement of trans detainees and prison conditions affect residents who enter the justice system; a visitor is exposed only if arrested, and the sources document no region-specific detention pattern.
